brief: MS maps $1.6T of 2027 hyperscaler/neocloud capex (up from $980bn in 2026, moderating to $1.8T, +14%, in 2028) to supplier revenue across roughly 50 companies. New lease-capex modeling adds $195bn in 2027 and $246bn in 2028, since leases bypass GAAP capex reporting; hyperscalers have disclosed $1.1T of leases not yet started. At a 65% absorption rate, this capex drives 5% of 2027 S&P 500 sales and about 25% of sales growth, lifting ex-AI 6.6% growth to 8.6%. AI names broadly, a 42-stock cohort MS calls Core to Thesis, drive 60% of 2027 S&P 500 sales growth and 78% of earnings growth, dominated by the Magnificent 7. Sector flow-through favors NVDA/AVGO/memory in semis, Synopsys/Cadence in EDA, Dell/HPE/STX/WDC/SNX in hardware, and VRT/ETN/GEV/CAT/CMI/EROC in power and cooling. Financing needs rise as 2027 marks hyperscalers' largest projected free-cash-flow deficit; high-quality balance sheets can absorb it while lower-rated neoclouds are more exposed. MS flags two downside risks: a 32 GW US power shortfall through 2028 that could delay deployments, and midterm-election policy pushback against data center construction, which it sees as most negative under a Democratic sweep.
